# Test fixtures

Everything the C test binaries read. All of it is checked in, so `task test` runs with no
network access, no model weights, and no Python, which is the point: if correctness
required the 1.56 TB checkpoint, correctness would not get checked.

Total is about 12 MB.

| path | bytes | read by | generated by |
|---|---:|---|---|
| `ops/` | ~2 MB | `test_ops` | `tools/emit_fixtures.py` |
| `ops/MANIFEST.json` | none | `test_ops` | same; lists fixtures and tolerances |
| `cache/` | ~200 KB | `test_cache` | `tools/make_cache_fixture.py` |
| `st/` | ~50 KB | `test_st` | `tools/make_st_fixture.py` |
| `ref_k3.json` | 6 KB | `k3_model` | `tools/make_k3_oracle.py` |
| `tiny_k3.bin`, `tiny_k3.json` | 9 MB | `k3_model` | same |
| `mxfp4.json` | 2.9 MB | `test_ops`, `tools/verify_expert.py` | `tools/emit_fixtures.py` |
| `golden/` | none | conformance comparison | `tools/ref_forward.py`, real weights |
| `gates/` | none | recorded gate output | the test binaries |
| `expert_trace.bin` | 800 KB | `tools/sim_cache.py` | a real model run with `--dump-cache-trace` |

## Regenerating

Every generator derives its output path from `tools/_paths.py`, so they all write here and
cannot drift apart. Regeneration needs PyTorch and the reference implementation in
`tools/k3_ref.py`:

```bash
python tools/emit_fixtures.py        # ops/ and mxfp4.json
python tools/make_k3_oracle.py       # ref_k3.json, tiny_k3.*
python tools/make_cache_fixture.py   # cache/
python tools/make_st_fixture.py      # st/
```

`expert_trace.bin` cannot be regenerated without the real checkpoint; capture a new one
with `./bin/k3 <model_dir> --dump-cache-trace tests/fixtures ...`.

## Why these fixtures and not simpler ones

Each is adversarial in a specific way, because the cheap version of each would pass
against a wrong implementation:

- **`ops/situ_glu.json`** spans |z| from 0.1 to 1000 so both soft caps saturate. In the
  near-linear regime `beta*tanh(z/beta) == z`, and an implementation with the caps
  omitted entirely passes.
- **`ops/kda_decay.json`** exports a spread of `A_log`, so an implementation indexing it
  per channel rather than per head fails. With one head, both index the same memory.
- **`ops/kda_recur*.json`** carry the module weights, not just inputs and outputs. A
  fixture recording only in/out of a randomly-initialised module is unreproducible: no
  implementation can match it, and it silently provides zero coverage.
- **`st/`** includes a bf16 1-D tensor, an f16 tensor of non-multiple-of-4 length, a
  packed U8 2-D tensor, a rank-0 scalar, and a tensor in a second shard, the shapes a
  reader handles by accident when it only ever sees well-behaved f32 matrices.
- **`cache/`** uses a deliberately non-conforming expert size. The real checkpoint's
  17,547,264 bytes happens to be an exact multiple of 4096, so O_DIRECT alignment holds
  there by coincidence; these fixtures do not let that coincidence hide a bug.
- **`cache/`** content is derived from the expert index, so slot aliasing, returning
  expert *a*'s bytes for expert *b*, is visible immediately instead of looking like
  plausible noise.
- **`mxfp4.json`** holds released checkpoint bytes, so the nibble order and the E8M0 scale
  exponent are checked against the released format rather than against this project's
  own assumptions about it.
- **`ref_k3.json`** is 13 layers, not 5. The Attention-Residual failure modes cannot
  appear until two blocks are complete and a third is in progress; a shallower fixture
  passes a broken implementation.
